Urban Regeneration and Development Fund – Call 3  
The Acquisitions Programme has been approved to include the Graiguecullen area of Carlow 
Town within Call 3. This funding acts as a dedicated revolving fund within each local authority 
so as to address the financial barrier and risk faced by local authorities in seeking to tackle long 
term vacant and derelict buildings and sites across URDF towns and cities. This fund is currently 
operational in Portlaoise where a number of properties have been considered and actioned 
therein.  
 
A survey of properties will not be undertaken in Graiguecullen with a view to entering them 
under this scheme.  
 
 
Vacancy / Regeneration Funding Schemes  
A Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is available for up to a maximum of €50,000, including 
VAT, for refurbishment of vacant properties for use as a principle private residence or to be made 
available for rent, including the conversion of a property which has not been used as residential 
heretofore.   A top-up grant of up to €20,000 is also available for properties which are derelict.  
To qualify for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant, properties must be: 
• 
Vacant for over 2 years and 
• 
Built before 2008

The Council can provide interest free funding of up to €80,000 (including VAT) per individual 
home delivered, to bring the property up to rental standard.  In return, the homes are leased to

Economic Development 
 
Junction 17 National Enterprise Park Marketing Campaign: 
The Business Support Unit is currently looking to appoint a marketing agency to develop and 
deliver a comprehensive, multi-channel campaign to promote J17 National Enterprise Park as a 
premier business location. Closing date for receipt of tenders is July 28th. 
 
Canal Road Business Park Portarlington: 
The four sites at Canal Road Business Park are currently on the market for sale. The sale of 
these sites is being advertised and managed by Tom McDonald Auctioneer.  Works at Canal 
Road Business Park have commenced. 
 
Market House Portarlington: 
 
The redevelopment of the Market House in Portarlington 
presents a significant opportunity to revitalize the town, 
stimulate economic activity, and enhance community life.  
Going forward the effective management will be critical to 
ensuring the long-term sustainability, accessibility, and 
relevance of the Market House.   
 
In this regard Laois County Council sought expressions of interest from Groups/ Bodies to 
manage and operate a Civic / Community and Tourist Information Hub, and to provide a 
Community / Social Enterprise space which would provide a tourist information point for the 
people of Portarlington and its hinterland. Options for the management of this space is currently 
ongoing. considered. It is envisaged that the building will be open and in use by September 
2025.

Tourism 
 
Old Fort Quarter Festival 2025 
 
The Old Fort Quarter Festival took place from 27th to 29th June.  Live music took place each 
night in the Performance and Events space with family and heritage events on Main Street and 
Fitzmaurice Place on Sunday 29th.  Events also took place in the County Library and Dunamaise 
Theatre. 
 
 
 
 
This year the festival committee partnered with Laois County Council’s climate action team with 
their Green Your Festival project to help reduce the environmental impact of the festival.  The 
Civil Defence medical support tents were powered by a battery storage system charged from 
renewal sources removing the need for diesel powered generators. 
 
 
 
National Steam Rally  
 
The launch of the National Steam Rally took place on Saturday 5th July.  The 61st National Steam 
Rally will take place on the August Bank Holiday weekend 2nd to 4th August on Cosby Estate 
Stradbally Co. Laois.

Just Transition Regenerative Tourism Fund 
 
The Regenerative Tourism Activator is currently working on the implementation of a network 
development roadmap, consisting of capacity building, network engagement, and mentorship. 
Through this eleven grantees are being supported with the delivery of their project or digital 
transformation.  
 
Two (2) new startups have been referred to the LEO for supports.  
Four (4)  businesses were supported with grant funding advice for the delivery of their project 
through other funding schemes. 
  
The Just Transition Regenerative Tourism Activator has been working as part of a 
multistakeholder group comprising of our EU counterparts from Portugal, Finland, Belgium, 
Czechia, Spain, Prague and Tim Hayes managing Director of the Hodson Bay Group, John 
Costello of the Midlands Regional Skills group and Offaly Local Development Company.  
 
The aim of the workshop was to discuss regenerative and sustainable smart tourism in the rural 
regions of our respective countries, and devise action plans for training going forward that would

WP 3 Midlands ICT Action Plan  
 
The Midlands ICT Network continues to deliver impactful events to support digital innovation, 
business development, and tech engagement across the region. 
 
The next phase of events resumes in August, focusing on finalising the Cyber Security and AI

These events mirror the successful formats from earlier sessions, but are adapted to local

Cristín Leach, art critic and writer has said of Bernadette’s work -  ‘Kiely reminds us that 
this is a whole world problem, not just one visible from her own front door, but another jolt 
to consciousness, a reminder that these paintings are a slow seeping cry to open our eyes 
and pay attention now.’ 
 
Participants work included drawings in charcoal and paintings using a pouring 
technique demonstrated by Bernadette.  There was an impressive wealth of 
waterscapes and figurative work which participants had produced over the previous 
four days as well as a documentary film by Amelia Caulfield with words by Bernadette 
narrating her childhood experience of floods on the Suir. 
 
Bernadette Kiely is an Irish visual artist renowned for her evocative depictions of the 
effects of environmental change.  Born in Carrick-on-Suir, Tipperary, she studied at 
Waterford Institute of Technology (SETU) and the Slade School of Fine Art, London. 
She worked in Graphic Design in London and New York before moving to 
Thomastown where she lives and works in her studio built by her predecessor the late 
painter Barrie Cooke.  Known for her powerful portrayals of the fragility of the natural 
world, the effects of flooding on land and human lives, have an enduring theme in her 
large-scale painting and drawing practice for over 20 years. She was a founder 
member of the Thomastown Environmental Association in the early 90’s. Bernadette 
is represented by Taylor Galleries, Dublin and is a member of Aosdána, the 
governmental body of artists deemed by their peers to be making a significant 
contribution to the arts in Ireland.  Recent exhibitions include Dreamtime Ireland, 
curated by Sean Lynch, VISUAL at Carlow Arts Festival 2025, RA Summer Exhibition 
2025, Royal Academy, London; RHA Summer Exhibition 2025, Royal Hibernian 
Academy, Dublin. 
 
Amelia Caulfield is a multidisciplinary artist, videographer, and arts facilitator with a 
passion for creating thoughtful, socially engaged experiences. Her practice spans 
public art, interactive installation, filmmaking, photography, printmaking, and 
community-led workshops. With a strong foundation in both theory and practice, 
Amelia holds a BA in Film and Documentary (GMIT), an MA in Social Practice and the 
Creative Environment (TUS) and is currently pursuing an MFA in Media at NCAD.  Her 
work explores how we relate to one another—through systems, communication, and 
lived experience—and is rooted in a desire to make space for honest expression, 
meaningful connection, and to give form to private or often-unspoken internal 
experiences.  Amelia brings a warm, grounded, and inclusive approach to facilitation, 
with years of experience delivering impactful workshops for organisations including 
the National Gallery of Ireland and Kilkenny Arts Office.  She is a member of several 
arts’ engagement panels, including Dublin City Council Culture Company, Kilkenny 
Leader Partnership, and the Kilkenny Arts Office, Art of Change Panel. Her work has 
been supported by ArtLinks, Kilkenny County Council, IMMA, and Kilkenny Leader. 
 
The exhibition will run until Saturday 30 August and we encourage all to attend.
